quest.title: Solitary Fragrance
quest.description: You finally ascended to the Jade Chamber, where Ningguang was waiting for you. She graciously accepted Paimon's gift, and offered one in return. You spoke at length about many things: deities, archons... and the Fatui...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x675, Mora x27500, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

talks.objective: Head to the location marked on the "paper snow"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There are so many talismans here! And some stacks of blank paper, too! Hmm, what are they for?

choices.text: It looks like they're copying the pattern on the talisman.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's seen this pattern before! But where...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon knows! It looks just like the Sigil of Permission that Childe gave you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, but how did a relic of the adepti end up in the hands of someone like Childe? Suspicious...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It's not just a relic...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, that's right. Cloud Retainer said that when the Lord of Geo created the Sigil of Permission, it wasn't to be used as some ol' relic...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Talismans like that were once used in the Archon War to channel divine powers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe the Fatui are copying the Sigil of Permission in hopes of achieving a similar effect?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Being able to channel divine power in battle... Whew, that sounds pretty dangerous.

choices.text: Seems the Fatui are definitely up to something.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And the plot thickens... We'll need to keep an eye on Childe, that's for sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, alright, that's enough sticking around here. We gotta go meet up with Zhongli soon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The last stop on our Rite of Parting preparations tour is... Dihua Marsh!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go! Paimon hates being late!

choices.text: Maybe this paper is only a snippet of a much bigger plan.
Maybe they're trying to reproduce a talisman.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Right on time. I myself only arrived moments ago.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Did you enjoy your visit to the Jade Chamber?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It was so biiig, and preetty, and expensive... Paimon's never seen such a fancy-schmancy place before!

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Indeed. It's second to none in all of Liyue.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Then you met with Ningguang, I trust? What did you talk about with her?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She's super rich and so generous. Paimon thinks she's very friendly!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Business people are always "friendly" when it suits their interests.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yeah, {M#his}{F#her} take on Ningguang is quite different from Paimon's. {M#He}{F#She} thinks that even the tactless Yuheng is more trustworthy than her.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Oh, so you also met with Keqing, then? What did she have to say?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She said, "The time of the adepti has long passed. If even the Liyue Qixing don't want to face that truth, then what future is there for Liyue?"

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Haha, no respect for the divine.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Indeed, contrary to the ever-bold Keqing, Ningguang is more of a businesswoman at heart, though they are both members of the Qixing.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Although she's friendly, there's no way of clearly discerning her true intentions.

choices.text: Ningguang is highly intelligent.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Yes, she has only relied on herself to rise to her current position. No ordinary person could ever achieve that.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: It's said that she's the one behind the constant expansion of the Jade Chamber. It's the second most important thing to her. Even if she ever gave up the position of Tianquan, she would never give up the Jade Chamber.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The Jade Chamber is only second? What's the most important thing to her then?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Why, Mora, of course.

choices.text: Makes sense.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: All Ningguang talked about was the Fatui this and the Fatui that... She said that after Rex Lapis was murdered, the Fatui have constantly been trying to sink their fingers into Liyue and that they aren't to be trusted.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: That is how the Fatui have always been. It doesn't surprise me in the least.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And now they are trying to reproduce the Sigil of Permission.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: No matter what they may be planning, you must be careful when dealing with the Fatui. Always be on your guard.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So is there anything we need to get for the Rite of Parting in Dihua Marsh?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Yes, as a matter of fact, there is. Today, we'll be gathering wild Glaze Lilies.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Glaze Lilies? But why did we come all the way out here? Doesn't the garden in Yujing Terrace have some? Even Qingce Village has Glaze Lilies...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh right, Paimon remembers that Madame Ping is always tending to flowers. Maybe we could ask her!

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: No, those lilies have all been gardened by people. They won't do at all.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Dihua Marsh used to be full of Glaze Lilies. It is a sort of joyful flower that listens to human song.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Before the Archon War, Dihua Marsh was all dry land and fertile soil. But the war caused landslides and the land was flooded, turning it into the marsh you see now. Nearly all the Glaze Lilies were wiped out.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Of course, there are some kinds of flowers that have been preserved and gardened by people in the city. But very few people know that Glaze Lilies may still be found in the wild.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Wild Glaze Lilies have the strongest fragrance. If we want to follow the true tradition of the Rite of Parting, we must grind up the wild lilies and place the powder in a censer of Everlasting Incense.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: But I'll need your assistance in gathering these flowers.

choices.text: You mean you need me to pick them?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: No, I need you to sing to them. Singing to the flowers will make them more fragrant.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Uh... so how good is your singing, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: I can hold a tune.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Why doesn't Paimon believe you...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: #We'll only know once {M#he}{F#she} starts singing.

choices.text: I'm a pro. Just step back and listen!
So you need me... to sing?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: ...That's correct. Your singing will surely bring out the strongest fragrance from the flowers.

choices.text: No surprises there.
Ningguang is highly ambitious.

talks.objective: Search for wild Glaze Lilies with Zhongli

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's time to sing. Whenever you're ready!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: *clears throat*...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Those weren't Glaze Lilies! Glaze Lilies wouldn't hit people!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Those flowers put up quite a fight...

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: This little monster is known as a "Whopperflower."

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Hmm... Strange. These petals look interesting.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: The Glaze Lilies used as a disguise were buried with the Whopperflower for too long. The result seems to have surprisingly potent medicinal value. Let's collect what we can of these petals.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well that's nice and all, but will those petals be useful for the Rite of Parting?

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, no.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, that's so lame...

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Excuse me...

dialogues.speaker: Ganyu
dialogues.text: Are you searching for Glaze Lilies?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, hey! It's... what's her face... Ah, Paimon can't remember...

choices.text: Greetings, Ganyu.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: Hello, traveler. I'm surprised you still remember my name.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: Ah! That reminds me, how was your visit to the Jade Chamber?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, it sure would've been better if you'd told us how to get up there!

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: Didn't I tell you the way!? Surely I did!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nope, we found the way on our own!

choices.text: It isn't a secret, so perhaps you just assumed we knew?

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: Oh, I see.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: (Uh-oh, I guess I really did forget to tell them...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, something seems a little off about Ganyu...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She's acting different from the first time we met... Where's her serious attitude now?

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: Ah, well, I met you at that time as an emissary of the Tianquan. But now, I am simply out on a stroll to see the flowers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You came all the way out here to see the flowers? Why not just enjoy the gardens of the city?

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: Yujing Terrace is where Rex Lapis parted from this world. If I strolled through those lonely gardens now, I wouldn't be able to bear it.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: Whenever my duties take me near Yujing Terrace these days, I draw the windows to block my view of the gardens.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... Sorry, we shouldn't have brought it up.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: No, it's quite alright. I just haven't processed my emotions yet.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: When the Archon War came to its end two thousand years ago, the first iteration of The Seven would gather in Liyue and drink with Rex Lapis. But five of those original seven had already passed before Rex Lapis — it's truly a changing of the guard.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So that means...

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: Yes. Now that the spirit of Rex Lapis has returned to the heavens, only Barbatos of Mondstadt remains of the first Seven.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: The other five, including Inazuma's Raiden Shogun, are no longer the same friends from two thousand years ago.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: Of the current Seven Archons, the youngest is Sumeru's God of Dendro. She is merely five hundred years old, whereas Rex Lapis was more than six thousand years old at the time of his passing.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: This means that Liyue had been under Rex Lapis' rule from the moment it was first founded 3,700 years ago. The city has never had to bid farewell to its deity...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: So, what do you think of this "farewell"?

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: Huh? This... This is a little sudden, I...

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: As a mortal, I've never dared to imagine a Liyue without Rex Lapis.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: But as an adeptus... I think I will eventually come to grips with reality. Since Rex Lapis has passed, the time of Liyue's contract with the gods and adepti has now reached its end.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Did you just say, "as an adeptus"?

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: Yes, I... I am a mix of human and Qilin. Adeptus blood flows through my veins. I fought for Rex Lapis and the city of Liyue during the Archon War.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: After the war ended, I signed a contract with Rex Lapis and took the position as secretary for the Qixing. I've continued those duties to this very day.

choices.text: So you're half Qilin? That explains the horns!

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: Well... uh, let's save that conversation for another day. You say that you are here looking for Glaze Lilies?

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: I also know where wild Glaze Lilies can be found. See, I've just picked one myself. Here, you may have it if you wish.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: We dare not refuse it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so did you sing a song before you picked the lily?

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: Indeed, I did. I know this tradition well. In fact, I sang a local Liyue ballad to it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, so you really know your stuff too! Thanks, Ganyu!

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: No, it is you who I should be thanking. If not for this chance meeting, I never thought that I would be able to contribute to the upcoming farewell for our ancient lord.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: If you would excuse me, I should return to my work now. Good luck.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: And that just about does it. Our preparations for the Rite of Parting are mostly finished.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Given the ease of picking Glaze Lilies, I think this was a fitting end to our tasks, in more ways than one.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Zhongli, you seem suited to working in agricultural development.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Paimon can already imagine him starting a business in Liyue.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Hah, I've had enough ventures in my life already.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Beginning a new undertaking is always difficult at first and requires no small amount of effort. And once business is at full steam, the stress of it all only wears away at you over time.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: So you must be careful to take the time to step back and reexamine yourself. If left unchecked, the wear and tear on your heart may go well past mending.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow! See, Zhongli sounds like he's already seen it all!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright, I think it's about time we head back to Liyue Harbor now.

choices.text: So you're how old!? That explains the forgetfulness!
Guess it was our fault for not asking.
Greetings, Yangu.

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: "Yangu"? Wh—Who's that?

response.speaker: Ganyu
response.text: Eh... You've completely forgotten my name, haven't you?

dialogues.speaker: Felix
dialogues.text: Ah, you're the consultant to Wangsheng Funeral Parlor — Mr. Zhongli, I presume?

dialogues.speaker: Felix
dialogues.text: The Millelith are watching our every move now. These are desperate times, we mustn't act rashly.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Desperate times?

dialogues.speaker: Felix
dialogues.text: The adepti of Jueyun Karst are finally on the move.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Do they intend to exercise force?

dialogues.speaker: Felix
dialogues.text: Most likely. I've heard that some members of the Qixing have already gone to meet them... Well, I say "meet," but it's more like they're attempting to stall the adepti outside the city.

dialogues.speaker: Felix
dialogues.text: However, both sides were quite obstinate, and hit an impasse.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: ...It seems inevitable, given the current situation.

dialogues.speaker: Felix
dialogues.text: The adepti do not acknowledge the Qixing, they only acknowledge the contracts of the Geo Archon. If the two sides come to blows, Liyue Harbor will be in no position to stop them.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: Surely the Liyue Qixing are not the sort to give in so easily?

dialogues.speaker: Felix
dialogues.text: Hmph. Their bone-headedness is known throughout the lands. Yet it's because of that obstinacy that mortals and adepti are now on the verge of conflict.

dialogues.speaker: Zhongli
dialogues.text: And what now? How is it that the Fatui have come under fire?

dialogues.speaker: Felix
dialogues.text: Ugh... that's all Ningguang's doing...

dialogues.speaker: Felix
dialogues.text: She proclaimed that "in these tumultuous times, the Millelith must rein in the actions of the Fatui."

dialogues.speaker: Felix
dialogues.text: Only now do they want to start keeping tabs on us? Huh! That's the Qixing for you!

dialogues.speaker: Felix
dialogues.text: Anyway, Mr. Zhongli, you're one of Childe's close associates. Please understand that your actions will reflect on us. Don't let anyone catch you off-guard.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks like things are about to boil over in Liyue Harbor...

choices.text: Is there anything we can do?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Do you intend to use your neutral identity as an intermediary between both sides? Or, will you use your sword to turn the balance?

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Neither path is an easy one...

response.speaker: Felix
response.text: Oh, by the way, Mr. Zhongli. We've heard that the Wangsheng Funeral Parlor has also been caught up in all this. They're currently squaring off with the authorities at the gates.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: Things are taking a turn for the worse...

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: I'm afraid I must leave now to handle things back at Wangsheng Funeral Parlor. I hope that Master Hu has been able to keep things under control for the moment.

response.speaker: Zhongli
response.text: #Consider your next course of action carefully, {NICKNAME}. If you're trying to prevent an explosion, it may be wisest to look for the fuse first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Phew... Having connections with the Fatui seems to be quite the double-edged sword.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So what did Zhongli mean by looking for the "fuse"?

choices.text: Childe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, Paimon gets it! If there's anyone that wants to see the whole city turned upside down, it's definitely him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: He must be waiting for the moment when no one is watching to do something really bad!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, where could we find him now?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Where would he go at a time like this?

choices.text: Follow me.
There's only one place he would go.
That ginger guy.
You know, Mr. More-Money-Than-Sense.
We can't just stand by and watch.
